event: Saturday of week four: Bea's alarm at six; she's out of bed before it stops, bouncing on her toes.
"Good luck charm," she says, and kisses you, and throws your jumper at you. "Up. Bank. Shouting."
The quad is white with frost; your breath smokes; the fell tops behind the academy are still snowy.

pictured.coverAfter: Every blade of grass is stiff with it, silver-white and crunching under your boots
pictured.outfit: dark coat over Bea's big cream cable-knit jumper, gloves, jeans and boots

event: At seven the novice fours carry their boats down from the boathouse, four rowers and a cox to each.
Bea's at the oar nearest the bow, in a Thornfield vest, her hair scraped back, grinning at you.
Morwenna stands on the jetty with a megaphone and a stopwatch, booming at them in a big calm voice.

pictured.coverAfter: She's at the oar nearest the bow. You find her at once. She's in a Thornfield
pictured.outfit: Thornfield rowing vest and leggings, hair scraped back in a tight knot

event: Shiv arrives at ten past with a flask and a woolly hat and stands beside you on the frosty bank.
The four pushes off; the oars catch, ragged at first, then together, and the boat leaps.

pictured.coverAfter: She comes down the path at a slouching amble, with her hands in her parka
pictured.outfit: navy parka over a grey hoodie, bright orange bobble hat

event: Shiv cups her hands and bellows something in Irish; Bea laughs and nearly catches a crab.
"What did you say?" you ask. Shiv grins. "Something about her arse. In a kind way."

memory.fact: Shiv bellowed at Bea in Irish from the bank: something about her arse, in a kind way.

event: You shout Bea's name, the way you promised; she can't wave, but she pulls harder, you can see it.
They row the length of the mere twice; the second time the boat runs clean, and Morwenna whoops.

memory.fact: Bea's novice four ran clean on its second length of the mere at training; Morwenna whooped.

event: Bea comes off the water steaming, soaked to the knees, blisters bleeding through her tape, glowing.
"Did you see it run?" she says. You say you saw. She kisses you, wet, in front of everyone.

memory.fact: After training Bea kissed Nala on the bank, wet from the water, in front of everyone.

event: "Go on," Bea says. "Nine. Your walk. Tell me everything after." She pushes you off, smiling.
Nine: Yusra is waiting at the Thornfield front door in boots and a dark wool coat, a rucksack on.
Her hair is plaited down her back; without her warden's badge she looks younger, and nervous.
"Morning, Nala," she says. "Harrow Fell. Two hours to the top. Can you manage?" You can.

memory.fact: Harrow Fell rises behind the academy; a path from the back gate reaches its cairned top in 2 hours.

event: You go out through the back gate; the path climbs at once, through bracken gone rusty with frost.
Yusra walks fast, her long legs eating the path; you keep up, breathing hard, and she slows.

pictured.coverAfter: She's standing on the step in boots and a dark wool coat, belted, with
pictured.outfit: dark wool coat belted, rucksack, old walking boots, hair in one long plait, no badge

event: At first you talk about easy things: Bea's boat, the essay, the infirmary's quiet nights.

memory.fact: On quiet infirmary nights the night porter brings Yusra a biscuit at three.

event: Halfway up you stop at a stile and look back: the academy small below, the mere bright as a coin.
Yusra hands you water from her rucksack. "I don't do this," she says. "Ask people to walk."

pictured.coverAfter: It's in the wall behind Thornfield's garden, an old wooden gate, stiff on its

event: "I'm glad you asked me," you say. Yusra looks at the view, and nods, and climbs on over the stile.
Higher up there's thin snow in the grass; your boots squeak in it, and Yusra laughs at the sound.
She tells you about walking on the moors above Leeds with her dad on Sundays, when she was small.

memory.fact: As a girl Yusra walked the moors above Leeds with her dad on Sundays, squeaking in the snow.

event: You say you can't remember who walked with you before; only that the fells feel right underfoot.

memory.fact: Nala can't remember who walked with her before, only that the fells feel right underfoot.
Nala can't remember who walked with her before, only that the fells feel right underfoot.

pictured.coverAfter: Halfway up, there's a stile in a stone wall.

event: Yusra stops and looks at you. "That's a lonely thing to carry," she says. "Whoever you were."
"Less lonely now," you say. Yusra holds your eyes a long moment, then walks on, closer to you.
The top: a cairn of grey stones, the wind hard and clean, snow on them, the whole valley below.
The mere, the academy, the village, the far fells going blue to the edge of the world.
Yusra puts a stone on the cairn, and hands you one; you put yours on top of hers.

memory.fact: Yusra and Nala each put a stone on Harrow Fell's cairn, Nala's on top of Yusra's.
Yusra and Nala each put a stone on Harrow Fell's cairn, Nala's on top of Yusra's.

event: The wind is fierce up here; your eyes stream; Yusra turns you by the shoulders out of it.
"Down there I'm your warden," she says, close, her hands still on your shoulders. "I keep lines."
"Up here?" you ask. Yusra looks at your mouth, then your eyes. "Up here it's just me," she says.

pictured.coverAfter: A heap of them, taller than you, built up by every walker who ever
pictured.setting: the cairn on top of Harrow Fell

event: She kisses you, once, slowly, her cold hands coming up to hold your face. Her mouth is warm.
You kiss her back; she makes a small sound, as if something long held has come loose, and holds on.
When she draws back her eyes are wet from the wind, or not. "That was over the line," she says.

memory.fact: On Harrow Fell's top Yusra said Up here it's just me, and kissed Nala: over the line, she said.
On Harrow Fell's top Yusra said Up here it's just me, and kissed Nala: over the line, she said.

event: "I don't care," Yusra says. "Not up here." She laughs, a little shakily, and takes your hand.
She leads you down off the top to Hollin Tarn, small and black, ringed with rushes, out of the wind.

memory.fact: Below Harrow Fell's top lies Hollin Tarn, small and black, ringed with rushes and out of the wind.

event: It's still and quiet there; you sit on a flat rock by the water, and she unpacks the rucksack.
Cheese sandwiches, two apples and a flask of sweet tea. "A ward," Yusra says. "Keeps it hot."
You laugh so hard you spill your tea; she watches you laugh, and her whole face is soft.

pictured.coverAfter: Hollin Tarn. Small, and black, and perfectly still, lying in a hollow below the

event: You eat looking at the tarn. Yusra sits close, her shoulder against yours, her hand in yours.
"I don't know what this is," she says. "I'm two years above you. I've been broken all summer."
"And you've got Bea," she says. "I've seen you two." You tell her the truth: Bea knows, and said go.
Yusra is quiet a while. "Bea Lindqvist," she says. "Huh." Then, softer: "That's generous of her."

memory.fact: Told Bea knows and said go, Yusra said: Bea Lindqvist. Huh. That's generous of her.
Told Bea knows and said go, Yusra said: Bea Lindqvist. Huh. That's generous of her.

event: "I can't promise anything," Yusra says. "I'm still mending." You say: mending takes a while.

memory.fact: At Hollin Tarn Yusra told Nala she can't promise anything; she's still mending.

event: She leans her head on your shoulder, by the black water, and closes her eyes, and breathes out.
You sit like that till the cold gets into your bones; she kisses you once more, quick, and stands.
On the way down she holds your hand till the back gate is in sight, and lets go there, gently.
At the gate she straightens her coat, and is your warden again: "Thank you, Nala. Go and get warm."
But at the Thornfield door she turns back, and her mouth twitches. "Same time next Saturday?"
Next Saturday is Bea's race; you say after the race, and Yusra nods. "After the race," she says.

memory.fact: Yusra asked Nala to walk again next Saturday; Nala said after Bea's race, and Yusra agreed.
Yusra asked Nala to walk again next Saturday; Nala said after Bea's race, and Yusra agreed.

event: Afternoon: you sleep an hour in 15, worn out; you wake to Bea sitting on the bed with two cocoas.
"Well?" says Bea. You tell her: the cairn, the tarn, the kiss. Bea's eyebrows go up and up.

memory.fact: Yusra and Nala each put a stone on Harrow Fell's cairn, Nala's on top of Yusra's.
On Harrow Fell's top Yusra said Up here it's just me, and kissed Nala: over the line, she said.

event: "Yusra Haddad kissed you on a mountain," Bea says. "Good. She needed it." She grins. "So did you."
You ask if she minds. Bea thinks about it honestly. "A bit, maybe. Not much. You came back to 15."

memory.fact: Told of Yusra's kiss, Bea said Good, she needed it; she minds a bit: You came back to 15.
Told of Yusra's kiss, Bea said Good, she needed it; she minds a bit: You came back to 15.

event: Evening: soup and toast in the kitchen; Yusra is at the far end with her books and glasses on.
She looks up once, across the room, only at you; then back at her page, her mouth soft.
You fall asleep early in 15, Bea's arm over you, your legs still aching from the fell.
A day at Hollowmere ends.
